From 0b16e69d17d8c35c5c9d5918bf596c75a44655d3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 17:20:36 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: x86: Use scratch field in MMIO fragment to hold small
 write values

When exiting to userspace to service an emulated MMIO write, copy the
to-be-written value to a scratch field in the MMIO fragment if the size
of the data payload is 8 bytes or less, i.e. can fit in a single chunk,
instead of pointing the fragment directly at the source value.

This fixes a class of use-after-free bugs that occur when the emulator
initiates a write using an on-stack, local variable as the source, the
write splits a page boundary, *and* both pages are MMIO pages.  Because
KVM's ABI only allows for physically contiguous MMIO requests, accesses
that split MMIO pages are separated into two fragments, and are sent to
userspace one at a time.  When KVM attempts to complete userspace MMIO in
response to KVM_RUN after the first fragment, KVM will detect the second
fragment and generate a second userspace exit, and reference the on-stack
variable.

The issue is most visible if the second KVM_RUN is performed by a separate
task, in which case the stack of the initiating task can show up as truly
freed data.

  ==================================================================
  BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in complete_emulated_mmio+0x305/0x420
  Read of size 1 at addr ffff888009c378d1 by task syz-executor417/984

  CPU: 1 PID: 984 Comm: syz-executor417 Not tainted 5.10.0-182.0.0.95.h2627.eulerosv2r13.x86_64 #3
  Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS rel-1.15.0-0-g2dd4b9b3f840-prebuilt.qemu.org 04/01/2014 Call Trace:
  dump_stack+0xbe/0xfd
  print_address_description.constprop.0+0x19/0x170
  __kasan_report.cold+0x6c/0x84
  kasan_report+0x3a/0x50
  check_memory_region+0xfd/0x1f0
  memcpy+0x20/0x60
  complete_emulated_mmio+0x305/0x420
  kvm_arch_vcpu_ioctl_run+0x63f/0x6d0
  kvm_vcpu_ioctl+0x413/0xb20
  __se_sys_ioctl+0x111/0x160
  do_syscall_64+0x30/0x40
  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x67/0xd1
  RIP: 0033:0x42477d
  Code: <48> 3d 01 f0 ff ff 73 01 c3 48 c7 c1 b0 ff ff ff f7 d8 64 89 01 48
  RSP: 002b:00007faa8e6890e8 EFLAGS: 00000246 ORIG_RAX: 0000000000000010
  RAX: ffffffffffffffda RBX: 00000000004d7338 RCX: 000000000042477d
  RDX: 0000000000000000 RSI: 000000000000ae80 RDI: 0000000000000005
  RBP: 00000000004d7330 R08: 00007fff28d546df R09: 0000000000000000

  R13: 0000000000000000 R14: 000000000040a200 R15: 00007fff28d54720

  The buggy address belongs to the page:
  page:0000000029f6a428 refcount:0 mapcount:0 mapping:0000000000000000 index:0x0 pfn:0x9c37
  flags: 0xfffffc0000000(node=0|zone=1|lastcpupid=0x1fffff)

The bug can also be reproduced with a targeted KVM-Unit-Test by hacking
KVM to fill a large on-stack variable in complete_emulated_mmio(), i.e. by
overwrite the data value with garbage.

Limit the use of the scratch fields to 8-byte or smaller accesses, and to
just writes, as larger accesses and reads are not affected thanks to
implementation details in the emulator, but add a sanity check to ensure
those details don't change in the future.  Specifically, KVM never uses
on-stack variables for accesses larger that 8 bytes, e.g. uses an operand
in the emulator context, and *all* reads are buffered through the mem_read
cache.

Note!  Using the scratch field for reads is not only unnecessary, it's
also extremely difficult to handle correctly.  As above, KVM buffers all
reads through the mem_read cache, and heavily relies on that behavior when
re-emulating the instruction after a userspace MMIO read exit.  If a read
splits a page, the first page is NOT an MMIO page, and the second page IS
an MMIO page, then the MMIO fragment needs to point at _just_ the second
chunk of the destination, i.e. its position in the mem_read cache.  Taking
the "obvious" approach of copying the fragment value into the destination
when re-emulating the instruction would clobber the first chunk of the
destination, i.e. would clobber the data that was read from guest memory.

Fixes: f78146b0f923 ("KVM: Fix page-crossing MMIO")

Reported-by: Yashu Zhang <zhangjiaji1@huawei.com>

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

Tested-by: Rick Edgecombe <rick.p.edgecombe@intel.com>

diff --git a/include/linux/kvm_host.h b/include/linux/kvm_host.h
index 34759a262b28..abb309372035 100644
--- a/include/linux/kvm_host.h
+++ b/include/linux/kvm_host.h
@@ -318,7 +318,8 @@ static inline bool kvm_vcpu_can_poll(ktime_t cur, ktime_t stop)
 struct kvm_mmio_fragment {
 	gpa_t gpa;
 	void *data;
-	unsigned len;
+	u64 val;
+	unsigned int len;
 };
 
 struct kvm_vcpu {
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/x86.c b/arch/x86/kvm/x86.c
index a03530795707..9bb9d7f078fc 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/x86.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/x86.c
@@ -8225,7 +8225,13 @@ static int emulator_read_write_onepage(unsigned long addr, void *val,
 	WARN_ON(vcpu->mmio_nr_fragments >= KVM_MAX_MMIO_FRAGMENTS);
 	frag = &vcpu->mmio_fragments[vcpu->mmio_nr_fragments++];
 	frag->gpa = gpa;
-	frag->data = val;
+	if (write && bytes <= 8u) {
+		frag->val = 0;
+		frag->data = &frag->val;
+		memcpy(&frag->val, val, bytes);
+	} else {
+		frag->data = val;
+	}
 	frag->len = bytes;
 	return X86EMUL_CONTINUE;
 }
@@ -8240,6 +8246,9 @@ static int emulator_read_write(struct x86_emulate_ctxt *ctxt,
 	gpa_t gpa;
 	int rc;
 
+	if (WARN_ON_ONCE((bytes > 8u || !ops->write) && object_is_on_stack(val)))
+		return X86EMUL_UNHANDLEABLE;
+
 	if (ops->read_write_prepare &&
 		  ops->read_write_prepare(vcpu, val, bytes))
 		return X86EMUL_CONTINUE;
@@ -11846,6 +11855,9 @@ static int complete_emulated_mmio(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)
 		frag++;
 		vcpu->mmio_cur_fragment++;
 	} else {
+		if (WARN_ON_ONCE(frag->data == &frag->val))
+			return -EIO;
+
 		/* Go forward to the next mmio piece. */
 		frag->data += len;
 		frag->gpa += len;

The patch fixes a use-after-free bug in KVM x86 MMIO emulation by copying small write values (≤8 bytes) into a scratch field within the MMIO fragment, preventing references to temporary on-stack variables during multi-fragment MMIO completion.

### Modifications per file

**include/linux/kvm_host.h**
- Added a `u64 val` scratch field to `struct kvm_mmio_fragment` to hold small write data inline.
- Changed the `len` field type from `unsigned` to `unsigned int` (cosmetic, no functional change).

**arch/x86/kvm/x86.c**
- `emulator_read_write_onepage()`: For write operations with `bytes ≤ 8`, copy the source data into `frag->val` and set `frag->data` to point to `&frag->val` (instead of pointing directly at the potentially on-stack source). Reads and larger writes keep the original behavior.
- `emulator_read_write()`: Added a `WARN_ON_ONCE` check to detect if a non-write or >8-byte access uses an on-stack source, returning `X86EMUL_UNHANDLEABLE` to catch future violations.
- `complete_emulated_mmio()`: Added a `WARN_ON_ONCE` check to ensure `frag->data` does not point to the scratch field `&frag->val` when advancing beyond the first fragment, returning `-EIO` to prevent accidental misuse.

### Relationships between modifications

The key relationship is that the new scratch field (`val` in `kvm_mmio_fragment`) is used in `emulator_read_write_onepage()` to store a copy of small write data, eliminating the need to keep a pointer to the caller’s (often on-stack) buffer across KVM_RUN exits. The two added warning checks serve as safety nets: the one in `emulator_read_write()` ensures that only small writes go through the scratch path, while the one in `complete_emulated_mmio()` guards against incorrectly treating a scratch-backed fragment as a pointer to externally managed memory during multi-fragment completion. Together, these changes eliminate the use-after-free scenario where a second KVM_RUN task accessed freed stack data from the original MMIO write.

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

**1. `include/linux/kvm_host.h`**
- **Structure enhancement:** Added a new `u64 val` field to `struct kvm_mmio_fragment`. This field acts as a scratch buffer to safely store the write value when the source data is small (≤ 8 bytes) and originates from a stack-local variable.
- **Type adjustment:** Changed the type of the `len` field from `unsigned` to `unsigned int` (cosmetic, for consistency).

- **In `complete_emulated_mmio()`:** Added a `WARN_ON_ONCE` check: if a fragment’s `data` pointer still points to `&frag->val` (indicating the scratch value has not been fully consumed), the function returns `-EIO` as an error guard.

- The core fix relies on the new `frag->val` scratch field. For small MMIO writes that may cross page boundaries, the fragment now stores the write value directly in the vCPU’s persistent `mmio_fragment` structure instead of pointing to the caller’s (potentially stack-allocated) memory. This prevents use-after-free because the data remains valid even when the second fragment is processed in a later `KVM_RUN` call by a different task.
- The changes in `emulator_read_write_onepage()` implement the actual copying into `frag->val` for small writes.
- The two `WARN_ON_ONCE` additions act as sanity checks: one prevents accidental use of stack data for unsupported cases (large writes or reads), and the other ensures that the scratch data is properly consumed in the completion path. These guards enforce the assumptions that make the fix safe and help catch future regressions.
- Overall, the modifications are tightly coupled: the struct extension provides the storage, the emulator code utilizes it for small writes, and the completion code verifies correct usage, all working together to eliminate the described use-after-free bug.

just writes, as larger accesses and reads are not affected thanks to
implementation details in the emulator, but add a sanity check to ensure

2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

This patch fixes a use-after-free bug in KVM's MMIO emulation when handling writes that cross a page boundary and both pages are MMIO. The fix involves copying small write values (≤8 bytes) into a new scratch field in the MMIO fragment, preventing dangling pointers to on-stack data.

### Modifications in Each File

**1. `include/linux/kvm_host.h`**
- Added a new `u64 val` field to `struct kvm_mmio_fragment`. This scratch field stores the to-be-written data for writes of 8 bytes or less, ensuring the data remains valid even if the original source is on the stack and freed.
- Changed `len` from `unsigned` to `unsigned int` for consistency.

**2. `arch/x86/kvm/x86.c`**
- **`emulator_read_write_onepage()`**: For write operations (`write == true`) with size ≤ 8 bytes, the function now:
  1. Initializes `frag->val` to zero.
  2. Points `frag->data` to `&frag->val`.
  3. Copies the actual value from `val` into `frag->val` using `memcpy`.
  
  This prevents `frag->data` from pointing directly at an on-stack variable that could be deallocated or overwritten before the MMIO request is fully processed.

- **`emulator_read_write()`**: Added a `WARN_ON_ONCE` safety check. If a read operation (`!ops->write`) or a write larger than 8 bytes uses an on-stack `val`, the emulation returns `X86EMUL_UNHANDLEABLE` (triggering a warning). This catches future violations where the emulator might incorrectly pass stack data for reads or large writes.

- **`complete_emulated_mmio()`**: Added another `WARN_ON_ONCE` in the branch that advances to the next fragment (when `frag->data == &frag->val`). If the scratch field is encountered during fragment completion (i.e., when moving to the second or later fragment), it returns `-EIO`. This ensures the scratch field is only used for the first fragment of a small write, not when advancing to subsequent fragments (which would corrupt the original copied data).

### Relationships Between the Changes

1. **Enabling the Fix**: The new `val` field in `kvm_mmio_fragment` provides a stable storage location for small write data. The x86 code uses this field to copy the value immediately, decoupling the fragment from the original (potentially stack-local) source.

2. **Safety Guards**: The two `WARN_ON_ONCE` checks in the x86 code complement the fix:
   - In `emulator_read_write()`, it prevents any code path from erroneously pointing an MMIO fragment at stack data for reads or large writes, which is not handled by the scratch field.
   - In `complete_emulated_mmio()`, it prevents accidental reuse of the scratch field when processing the second fragment of a page-split access. The scratch value is only valid for the first fragment; advancing to the next fragment must use the original `frag->data` pointer (which now points to scratch only for the first fragment of a small write).

3. **Overall Effect**: The patch eliminates the root cause of the use-after-free (dangling pointer to stack memory) by copying data into the fragment's own memory. The warning checks serve as fail-safes to ensure the fix’s assumptions (only small writes use the scratch field, only the first fragment uses it) are not violated by future code changes.

When exiting to userspace to service an emulated MMIO write, copy the
to-be-written value to a scratch field in the MMIO fragment if the size
of the data payload is 8 bytes or less, i.e. can fit in a single chunk,
instead of pointing the fragment directly at the source value.

This fixes a class of use-after-free bugs that occur when the emulator
initiates a write using an on-stack, local variable as the source, the
write splits a page boundary, *and* both pages are MMIO pages.  Because
KVM's ABI only allows for physically contiguous MMIO requests, accesses
that split MMIO pages are separated into two fragments, and are sent to
userspace one at a time.  When KVM attempts to complete userspace MMIO in
response to KVM_RUN after the first fragment, KVM will detect the second
fragment and generate a second userspace exit, and reference the on-stack
variable.

The issue is most visible if the second KVM_RUN is performed by a separate
task, in which case the stack of the initiating task can show up as truly
freed data.
